key_insight: Goku introduces a million-scale, instruction-aligned video editing dataset that goes beyond simple appearance changes to support multi-task and structural video edits. This expands video editing benchmarks toward more realistic, complex creative control.
problem_solved: Current instruction-based video editing datasets are too narrow, mostly covering single-task appearance editing. They do not adequately represent real-world editing needs such as multi-step transformations and precise subject motion control.
method: Built Goku, a 2 million-pair video editing dataset with high-quality instruction-video alignment.
Extended the task scope from basic appearance edits to multi-task and structural manipulations, including controlled subject movement.
Designed the dataset to serve as a benchmark for evaluating more capable instruction-based video editing models.
impact: This dataset gives researchers a much richer training and evaluation resource for instruction-based video editing. It can help drive models that understand complex user prompts and perform more realistic, controllable video transformations.

paper_title: Goku: A Million-Scale Universal Dataset and Benchmark for Instruction-Based Video Editing
paper_authors: Sen Liang, Cong Wang, Zhentao Yu, Fengbin Guan, Zhengguang Zhou
